prompt: Write the body (about 120 words) of a letter of representation from a personal injury lawyer to an auto insurer. The client was hurt in a low-speed head-on collision. Ask that all contact go through the law firm, ask for the policy limits, and ask the insurer to keep all evidence. No salutation, no signature, no names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1424; do not mention it.)
text:
I am writing to advise that this office now represents the injured party in connection with the low-speed head-on collision described in the claim you have opened. Our client has sustained injuries that are being evaluated and treated, and we ask that your company direct all further communication regarding this matter to our office rather than to our client. Please do not contact our client directly by telephone, mail, or in person.

To allow us to assess the claim properly, we request that you provide the bodily injury and property damage limits of every policy that may apply to the at-fault driver and vehicle, including any excess or umbrella coverage, along with written confirmation of those limits. We also ask that you identify the adjuster assigned to the file.

We further request that your company preserve all evidence relating to the incident. This includes the claim file, photographs, recorded statements, vehicle inspection reports, repair estimates, telematics or event data recorder information, police reports, and any other materials in your possession or control. Please suspend any routine deletion or disposal of such records while the claim remains open.

We look forward to your prompt written response.
